description: The whole body of both legal routes, in ONE <section>. Block 0 is a meta line + h1 with no body; every later block is an h2 + an HTML body.

requiresOperatorSuppliedText.note: HARD GATE. The real text is another organisation’s legal instrument (see assets/asset-roles.json#nonAssetContentBans.realLegalText). The STRUCTURE is reusable; the TEXT must be replaced wholesale, never reused or paraphrased.

motion.notes: MEASURED: document.getAnimations() is [] on the original and no element in the page body has a transition. Zero motion of any kind.

responsive.base: pt-18 pb-14, block gap 48px, heading->body gap 12px

knownUpstreamDefects: BOTH legal routes still ship the unmodified Next.js/Sanity starter boilerplate as their meta description: "A statically generated blog example using Next.js and Sanity." The original never replaced it. Reproduced on purpose.
notes: There is NO prose/typography system. All vertical rhythm comes from exactly two flex row-gaps. Paragraph margins, list markers, list indentation and li gaps are all 0 via Tailwind preflight. Do NOT add `prose`, `space-y-*`, `list-disc` or `pl-*`.
No borders, brackets, buttons, gradients, radii or shadows anywhere on these routes.

<strong> is styled only by preflight `b,strong{font-weight:bolder}`, which against the surrounding weight 300 resolves to the real terraneSans 400 face. Never use font-bold here — there is no 500/600/700 webfont.

The original ships `

` wrapping further

/

    children — invalid nesting the browser unnests anyway. The clone uses a
    wrapper, which is visually identical.
Block counts: /terms-of-service = 24 blocks (title + 23 sections); /cookie-policy = 8 blocks (title + 7 sections).
